question: Since 2002, serious nitrate pollution has been recorded in Mazara del Vallo, Sicily, in the water distributed via the municipal aqueduct in the Trasmazzaro-Tonnarella district and, since 27 July 2023, also in the east of the town. Currently, one third of the city is being supplied with water that is undrinkable, with nitrate levels over twice the threshold values1.

The plan to install a water purifier envisaged by the municipal council solely to serve the Trasmazzaro-Tonnarella district would only alleviate the problem rather than solving its root cause. In fact, the cause of the pollution is still not clear and has not been properly investigated by the competent authorities.

This inertia on the part of the public authorities and the failure to safeguard water quality may contravene Directive 98/83/EC, under which Member States must ensure that water is clean and pure, Directive 2000/60/EC, which provides for special protection for bodies of water used to source drinking water, and Directive (EU) 2020/2184, which deals with the supply chain and access to water for vulnerable groups.
Can the Commission answer the following questions: 1.
Has it ever received reports relating to this specific case?
Will it check that the local and regional authorities are complying with the aforementioned EU legislation?
Will it push for the causes of the pollution to be eliminated, the identification of those responsible and the payment of compensation?
On 28 November 2023, a nitrate-in-water concentration of 111.9 mg/l was detected in the water being distributed.
answer: The quality of drinking water in the EU is regulated by the recast Drinking Water Directive (DWD) (2), which obliges Member States to ensure that drinking water is wholesome and clean. In addition, the Water Framework Directive (WFD) (3) provides special protection for water bodies used for the abstraction of drinking water. 1.

Regarding the nitrate levels in the water supplied in Mazara del Vallo, the Commission has not received any information, nor has it been alerted with regard to any parametric exceedances. 2. Under the recast DWD, Member States have to ensure compliance with drinking water quality standards by monitoring the nitrate parameter and reporting annually to the Commission on any exceedance.

Without prejudice to the Commission’s role as guardian of the Treaties, the primary responsibility for the implementation of the directive and protection of water quality lies on Member States (4). 3. Under the WFD, Member States had to take all measures necessary to bring surface water bodies to good ecological status or potential and to good chemical status, by 2015.

Time related exemptions are possible until 2027, subject to sound justification in the River Basin Management Plans (RBMP). The Commission is assessing the third cycle RBMP, covering the period December 2021 — December 2027 and will publish in the Summer of 2024 a report including recommendations for each Member State.
